solutions.title: Brute force pair scan
solutions.strategy: Check every pair of distinct indices until a pair sums to the target.

timeComplexity.explanation: For each index i, the algorithm scans every later index j. The number of pair checks is n - 1 plus n - 2 down to 1, which is proportional to n squared.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The algorithm stores only loop counters and the returned pair. It does not allocate auxiliary storage proportional to the input length.

solutions.title: One-pass complement map
solutions.strategy: Store seen values with their indices and check whether the current value's complement has already appeared.

timeComplexity.explanation: The array is scanned once. Each hash lookup and insertion is expected constant time, so the expected total time grows linearly with the input length.

spaceComplexity.explanation: If the matching pair appears late, the map can store an index for nearly every earlier value, so auxiliary memory grows linearly in the worst case.
